scams.name: Li River Cruise Fake-Ticket & 'Upgrade' Scams
scams.description: The Li River (Lijiang) cruise from Guilin to Yangshuo is China's iconic karst-landscape boat trip — 83 km of photogenic peaks between Zhujiang and Yangshuo, 4 hours one-way. The legitimate tourist-class ticket is ¥215 adult via the Guilin Zhujiang Pier or Magu Pier official booking; deluxe/VIP boats cost ¥310–¥450. The scam variants: (1) hotel-lobby booths quote ¥500–¥800 per person for 'standard' cruise + 'private guide' + 'hotel pickup' bundles where the cruise itself is actually ¥215; (2) street touts near Guilin Railway Station sell 'discount tickets' on boats that turn out to be local bamboo-raft boats, not the full Li River cruise; (3) 'upgraded' boats marketed at ¥400+ that are actually the standard boats. r/China 'Common scams you should know before traveling to China' (comments/2aqq6l) documents the broader Chinese cruise-ticket overpricing pattern. r/travelchina 'Are tours in China still sketchy and make you go shopping?' (comments/1k85j1d, 2025) confirms the 2025 continuation. The legitimate booking channel is the Guilin Lijiang Cruise website via Trip.com / Ctrip / Viator, or the Magu Pier ticket office directly. r/chinatravel 'Traveling to China - What I learned' (comments/1fjwbtc, 2024) notes the Yangshuo rural-area scam density: 'in some rural areas (we went to Yangshuo) they tried to scam us a lot.' For older travelers, the practical playbook: (1) book the standard 4-hour cruise via Trip.com, Viator, or Ctrip at ¥215–¥310 per person; (2) avoid hotel-lobby 'Li River cruise package' at ¥500+ — all are commission markups; (3) the cruise departs from Magu Pier (40 km south of Guilin) — pre-arranged transfer is ¥50–¥80 per person shared (bus); (4) at Yangshuo arrival, pre-book your hotel pickup rather than accepting touts at the dock; (5) AVOID any 'all-in-one Guilin + Yangshuo tour' under ¥600 per person total — real cost is ¥800–¥1,200 with honest operators.
scams.avoidance: Book standard 4-hour Li River cruise via Trip.com, Viator, or Ctrip at ¥215–¥310 per person Avoid hotel-lobby packages at ¥500+; buy the cruise ticket only, then pre-book hotel transfer separately Magu Pier transfer bus from Guilin ~¥50–¥80 per person shared Pre-book Yangshuo hotel pickup; don't accept touts at Yangshuo dock Reject any 'all-in-one Guilin+Yangshuo tour' under ¥600 per person — shopping stops guaranteed
scams.location: Guilin hotel lobbies, Magu Pier, Zhujiang Pier booking booths, Yangshuo arrival docks

scams.name: Yangshuo Bamboo Raft & Photo-Trap Scams
scams.description: Yangshuo's short bamboo-raft trips on the Yulong River are charming and legitimate — ¥150–¥200 per 2-person raft for a 90-minute float is the fair rate. The scam variants: (1) tout at West Street offers 'discount raft ¥80' that turns out to be 30 minutes in a stagnant backwater; (2) 'traditional cormorant fishing' at ¥80 per person is actually a fake cormorant-show where the birds are chained and no real fishing happens; (3) 'photo with fisherman' (the old man with straw hat + two cormorants) on the Li River costs ¥20–¥50 per photo — the fisherman is posed for tourist photos, not actually fishing, and has been documented on r/China 'Common scams you should know before traveling to China' (comments/2aqq6l) as essentially a photo-tout operation. r/chinatravel 'Traveling to China - What I learned' (comments/1fjwbtc, 2024) documents the rural-tourist-scam density: 'in some rural areas (we went to Yangshuo) they tried to scam us a lot even tho we travelled with a Chinese friend. r/travelchina 'Are tours in China still sketchy and make you go shopping?' (comments/1k85j1d, 2025) confirms the bamboo-raft 'tour' scams continue in 2025. For older travelers, the practical guide: (1) book Yulong River bamboo-raft ride via a guesthouse that has posted prices — ¥150–¥200 per 2-person raft for the full 90-min route is fair; (2) for cormorant fishing, the only 'authentic' experience is a pre-dawn fisherman on the Li River (not staged shows) — most tourists are better off skipping; (3) NEVER accept a tout's 'discount raft' offer on West Street; (4) West Street (Xi Jie) itself has become 85% tourist shops with inflated pricing — walk to the adjacent residential streets for honest food; (5) Yangshuo day-trip from Guilin: train to Guilin North, bus to Yangshuo ¥25 (1.5h) or stay overnight at a guesthouse rather than day-trip tour.
scams.avoidance: Book Yulong River raft via guesthouse with posted prices (¥150–¥200 per 2-person for full 90-min route) Skip 'cormorant fishing shows' — they are staged performances, not authentic Refuse 'photo with fisherman' requests on the Li River cruise Walk one block off West Street for honest food at residential restaurants Stay overnight in Yangshuo rather than day-trip tour — more authentic and cheaper
scams.location: Yulong River Yangshuo bamboo-raft docks, West Street tourist strip, cormorant-fishing 'show' pickup points

scams.name: Guilin Airport (KWL) & Railway Station Taxi Overcharge
scams.description: Guilin Liangjiang International Airport (KWL) is 30 km south of the city centre. The legitimate metered taxi fare is ¥100–¥130 (45 min). Unofficial drivers at arrivals and Railway Station quote 'fixed prices' of ¥200–¥300. r/travelchina 'Taxi drivers in China airports and train station' (comments/1ks12o9, 2025) is the 2025 China-wide airport-taxi scam anchor applicable at KWL: 'They are scams and trying to overcharge you. It's unbearable. Go straight to the real taxi stand.' r/travelchina 'Who are all the guys offering rides at the airport?' (comments/1fn0zz1, 2024) confirms the universal rule. DiDi operates at KWL with English interface; the official rideshare pickup is at the marked zone. The Airport Shuttle Bus to Guilin City runs ¥25 per person (45 min). For Guilin Railway Station and Guilin North Railway Station arrivals, taxi touts similarly quote 2–3x metered rates — the real city-centre taxi fare from either station is ¥15–¥30. For older travelers, the practical guide: (1) take the Airport Shuttle Bus (¥25, 45 min) if you arrive during daytime hours; (2) install DiDi before flying for app-regulated fares at the official pickup zone; (3) if taking a licensed taxi, say 'da biao' (打表) and expect ¥100–¥130 KWL-to-centre; (4) at Guilin Railway Station, walk past taxi touts to the official outdoor rank; (5) for Yangshuo transfer from KWL, the Guilin Airport bus to Yangshuo runs ¥50 (90 min) — much cheaper than a ¥300+ taxi quote.
scams.avoidance: Airport Shuttle Bus KWL to Guilin City: ¥25, 45 min DiDi with international-number sign-up at official rideshare pickup zone Licensed taxi: 'da biao' (打表) and expect ¥100–¥130 KWL-to-centre KWL-to-Yangshuo airport bus: ¥50, 90 min (scam-free) Photograph taxi plate number from rear windscreen before boarding
scams.location: Guilin Liangjiang International Airport (KWL) arrivals, Guilin Railway Station taxi rank, Guilin North Railway Station

scams.name: Guilin Tea House & Guiyang Fermented Rice Wine Scams
scams.description: Guilin's compact tourist core around Elephant Trunk Hill, Seven Star Park, and the Two Rivers and Four Lakes promenade has a gentler variant of the nationwide tea-house scam. The approach: fluent-English strangers at Elephant Trunk Hill or the Two Rivers waterfront invite visitors to a 'traditional Guangxi tea ceremony' or 'fermented rice wine tasting' at a side-street venue. Bill: ¥800–¥3,000 per person. The scam is less organised than Beijing/Shanghai but follows the same script. r/China 'Common scams you should know before traveling to China' (comments/2aqq6l) places the Guilin tea variant in the broader China-wide ring. Guilin's specific regional version pitches 'Guangxi tea' or 'fermented rice wine' (the Dong and Zhuang ethnic-minority specialities) instead of green tea — the product is real but sold at 20–40x residential rates. r/travelchina 'I never knew I would get scammed in China' (comments/1cxb3pv, 2024) documents the cross-city consistency of the script. r/travelchina 'Unpleasant but necessary topic: scams in China' (comments/9rfh7c) places Guilin on the short list of Chinese tourist cities running the tea-invite pattern. For older travelers visiting Guilin's old-city scenic areas, the rule: walk past any stranger who approaches in fluent English with invitations to tea, rice wine, ethnic-minority village visits, or cultural experiences. For genuine Guangxi tea, Guilin Tea Research Institute has a visitor centre with posted prices. For authentic Dong and Zhuang ethnic-minority cultural experience, the genuine option is a booked overnight trip to Longji Rice Terraces or Ping'an Zhuang village — book via Trip.com or Viator with licensed operators, not via a stranger's side-street invitation.
scams.avoidance: Walk past any stranger at scenic areas with 'bu yao xie xie' For Guangxi tea, visit Guilin Tea Research Institute visitor centre (posted prices) For authentic ethnic-minority experience, book Longji Rice Terraces or Ping'an overnight via Trip.com/Viator Never follow a stranger to a side-street 'tasting' venue Pay with credit card for chargeback leverage if trapped
scams.location: Guilin Seven Star Park approach, Two Rivers and Four Lakes waterfront, Elephant Trunk Hill ticket office queue, Guilin old town pedestrian streets

scams.name: Longji Rice Terraces Minority Village Tour Overcharge
scams.description: Longji Rice Terraces (90 km north of Guilin) is a genuinely spectacular UNESCO-candidate landscape with Zhuang and Yao ethnic-minority villages. Hotel-concierge day-trip packages charge ¥400–¥800 per person; the self-guided alternative via public bus + entry ticket + lunch costs ¥150–¥250. The scam variants: (1) hotel concierge marks up 2–3x for a tour that includes 'Miao long-hair show' that is staged for tourists; (2) 'ethnic-minority home-stay' packages at ¥600+ per night are modern guesthouses rebranded; (3) 'hand-loom weaving demonstration' includes forced purchase of ¥200–¥500 woven scarves at 3–5x market price. r/China 'Government facilities in travel tour scams? (Jade, TCM)' (comments/1hfcgv5, 2024) documents the pattern extends to ethnic-minority tour stops. r/travelchina 'Are tours in China still sketchy and make you go shopping?' (comments/1k85j1d, 2025) confirms 2025 continuation. The authentic Longji experience: spend one night at Ping'an Zhuang or Dazhai, walk the terrace trails at sunrise, eat at the guesthouse, avoid the 'cultural shows.' r/chinatravel 'Traveling to China - What I learned' (comments/1fjwbtc, 2024) references the Yangshuo-area scam density that extends north to Longji. For older travelers who want Longji Rice Terraces: (1) book a 1-night guesthouse at Ping'an Zhuang or Dazhai directly via Ctrip / Trip.com / Booking.com (¥300–¥600 per room); (2) take bus from Guilin Qintan Bus Station to Longji (¥25, 2.5h) or licensed tour van (¥80–¥120); (3) pay Longji entrance ticket ¥80 at the gate; (4) AVOID day-trip tours at ¥400+ — a self-guided overnight costs ¥400 total per person; (5) skip 'cultural shows' and 'hand-loom demonstrations' — they pay commissions to the tour operators who bring you there.
scams.avoidance: Book Ping'an Zhuang or Dazhai guesthouse direct (¥300–¥600/night via Ctrip/Trip.com/Booking) Bus Guilin Qintan to Longji ¥25 (2.5h) or tour van ¥80–¥120 Longji entrance ticket ¥80 at gate Skip 'cultural shows' and 'hand-loom demonstrations' — all commission-driven Total self-guided Longji overnight ~¥400 per person all-in vs ¥400+ day-trip tour
scams.location: Ping'an Zhuang Village, Dazhai Yao Village, Jinkeng Terraces; hotel-concierge 'Longji day-trip' packages

scams.name: Guilin Night Market & Tourist-Menu Restaurant Overcharge
scams.description: Guilin's compact tourist core has a modest tourist-menu restaurant problem. The Zhengyang Pedestrian Street (city centre, east of Two Rivers) and the waterfront restaurants around the Two Rivers and Four Lakes use laminated-English-photo menus with prices inflated 50–100% over residential rates. Common overcharge: Guilin rice noodles (Guilin's signature dish, normally ¥8–¥15 per bowl) served at ¥30–¥50 at tourist-strip venues; 'beer fish' (Yangshuo specialty) at ¥180–¥300 at Zhengyang when it costs ¥80–¥150 at Yangshuo residential restaurants; 'Taro taro' dessert at ¥40 when the residential price is ¥10–¥15. r/travelchina 'Unusual experience/possible scam on China trip' (comments/1nqcbht, 2025) documents the 2025 general tourist-menu pattern. For older travelers, the practical guide: (1) walk one block off Zhengyang Pedestrian Street for honest Guilin rice noodle shops; community favourites: Chong Shan Rice Noodle (¥10), Yi Cun Yi Wei (¥12); (2) for beer fish, wait until Yangshuo and eat at a residential restaurant rather than a Guilin tourist-strip version; (3) avoid the 'night market' tourist stalls with English signs and photos — the same dishes at 2–3x price; (4) any restaurant with a tout outside in English is targeting tourists — the restaurants one street back, with Chinese-only menus, serve locals at fair pricing.
scams.avoidance: Walk one block off Zhengyang for honest Guilin rice noodle (¥8–¥15) Eat beer fish in Yangshuo residential restaurants, not Guilin tourist strip Community favourites: Chong Shan Rice Noodle, Yi Cun Yi Wei Skip night-market tourist stalls with English signs Any restaurant with English-speaking tout outside is targeting tourists — walk past
scams.location: Zhengyang Pedestrian Street, Central Square night market, tourist restaurants around Two Rivers and Four Lakes

scams.name: Guilin Hotel Tour-Desk Commission & 'All-Inclusive' Upsells
scams.description: Guilin hotels across all tiers have commission arrangements with local tour operators that pay 20–40% kickback on every booking. The result: 'Li River cruise + Yangshuo + cormorant show' packaged tours sold at hotel lobbies for ¥600–¥1,200 per person cost 2–3x what independent booking via Trip.com or Viator delivers. r/China 'Government facilities in travel tour scams? (Jade, TCM)' (comments/1hfcgv5, 2024) documents the full pattern: hotel concierge endorses a specific operator; the operator's tour includes 'jade museum,' 'silk factory,' or 'rice wine distillery' stops where the hotel receives additional commissions on purchases; 20–30% of tour time is shopping. r/travelchina 'Are tours in China still sketchy and make you go shopping?' (comments/1k85j1d, 2025) confirms this operates unchanged in 2025. r/chinatravel 'Traveling to China - What I learned' (comments/1fjwbtc, 2024) captures the Guilin-specific concern: 'in some rural areas (we went to Yangshuo) they tried to scam us a lot' — the rural day-trip ecosystem operates hand-in-hand with Guilin hotel commissions. For older travelers, the defensive playbook: (1) NEVER book day trips, cruises, or excursions via hotel concierge or lobby tour booths in Guilin; (2) book direct via Trip.com / Viator / GetYourGuide / Tiqets with operators that have 'zero shopping stops' verified in writing; (3) licensed small-group operators include China Highlights, Viator Guilin, and Ctrip's vetted partners; (4) expect ¥400–¥600 per person honest Li River cruise + Yangshuo + return transport; anything above is hotel-concierge commission markup; (5) if a hotel presents a tour verbally at 'special price,' ask them to show the operator's independent website — if they can't, walk away.
scams.avoidance: NEVER book day trips via hotel concierge or lobby tour booths Book direct: Trip.com, Viator, GetYourGuide, Tiqets with 'zero shopping stops' verified in writing Licensed operators: China Highlights, Viator Guilin, Ctrip vetted partners Expect ¥400–¥600 per person honest day trip; above is commission markup If concierge presents verbal 'special price,' demand the operator's independent website
scams.location: Guilin hotel lobbies (particularly budget and mid-range), hotel concierge booking desks, partnered tour operator booths
